title: A Fault-Tolerant Million Qubit-Scale Distributed Quantum Computer
problem: Large-scale quantum computers require distributing qubits across multiple dilution refrigerators to overcome cooling constraints, but this creates slow and erroneous inter-DR entanglement and makes baseline error handling ineffective due to increased gate operations and communication latency.
motivation: Million qubit-scale quantum computers are essential to realize quantum supremacy and unlock practical quantum computing applications.
method: The paper proposes a fault-tolerant architecture designed for distributed quantum computers spanning multiple dilution refrigerators. It addresses inter-DR entanglement challenges and reduces error correction communication latency through improved quantum error handling mechanisms optimized for multi-DR systems.
key_novelty: Fault-tolerant design specifically optimized for million-qubit distributed quantum systems that efficiently handles inter-DR communication and error correction latency.
contributions: Fault-tolerant quantum error correction framework for multi-DR quantum computers
Solutions to slow and erroneous inter-DR entanglement in large-scale distributed systems
Reduced error decoding and correction latency across distributed refrigerated units
Architecture enabling scalable million-qubit quantum computing
limitations: Specific limitations of the proposed approach are not discussed in the abstract.
